newsitem.title: USA: Port Authority still mulling World Trade Ctr fate.
newsitem.headline: Port Authority still mulling World Trade Ctr fate.

text.p: While the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey is continuing to pare away non-core assets, the fate of its World Trade Center remains undecided, Authority officials said Thursday.

"We are continuing to pursue opportunities for our remaining non-core facilities through private management or outright sale," Authority Chief Financial Officer Charles McClafferty told attendees at The Bond Buyer's Investor Forum.

"We are studying methods to maximize the value of the World Trade Center, and looking at privatization alternatives to continued Port Authority ownership and operation with the goal of maximizing the value of the asset to the agency," McClafferty said.
Port Authority Treasurer Bruce Bohlen said the authority has been working with JP Morgan Securities Inc for approximately a year to weigh the authority's options concerning the Trade Center.

"Our board of commissioners are involved in reviewing those recommendations and, as (McClafferty) said, it's a little hard to say hard to say when the decision might be made, but it's under active review," Bohlen said. "What we are looking at is an outright sale, a long-term net lease, or asset management where we retain ownership and someone comes in to manage...I think those are really the three options that are being looked at."
The list of assets the authority has privatized or sold off includes the Vista Hotel in New York.
